title: Not Nice: Stop People Pleasing, Staying Silent, & Feeling Guilty... And Start Speaking Up, Saying No, Asking Boldly, And Unapologetically Being Yourself
author: Dr. Aziz Gazipura
target_audience: Adults who struggle with people-pleasing tendencies
Individuals who find it hard to say no or express themselves
Professionals seeking to build assertiveness and confidence
Anyone desiring to set healthier boundaries and be more authentic
core_themes: The dangers of chronic niceness and people-pleasing
Overcoming guilt and fear associated with saying no
Building self-worth independent of others’ approval
Transforming relationships through honesty and boundaries
primary_purpose: To help readers recognize and break free from deeply ingrained patterns of excessive niceness—such as people-pleasing, over-apologizing, and suppressing needs—in order to live a more confident, unapologetically authentic, and fulfilling life.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, direct, supportive, and sometimes humorous
structure_format.organization: Structured into chapters focused on causes of niceness, consequences, and a practical step-by-step program for change
features: Personal stories and client case studies

key_concepts_lessons: Being 'nice' can be a harmful coping mechanism rooted in fear of rejection or abandonment.
People-pleasing often leads to resentment, inauthenticity, and a loss of self-identity.
Saying no, setting boundaries, and expressing desires are essential for mental health and fulfillment.
Guilt and fear are natural but manageable obstacles on the path to assertiveness.
True kindness and healthy relationships require honesty and self-respect.
Growth happens by tolerating discomfort and challenging old beliefs about approval and conflict.
notable_features: Blends psychological insights with practical strategies
Emphasis on both inner mindset and external actions
Includes numerous self-reflection questions and exercises
Written by a clinical psychologist with expertise in social confidence
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2017, during a period of increased attention to boundaries, self-assertion, and mental health, as more people began to recognize the costs of chronic people-pleasing in modern work and relationships.
reception_impact: Widely praised by readers struggling with people-pleasing and low self-confidence
Appreciated for its actionable advice, relatable tone, and real-world examples
Popular in self-help, therapy, and personal development communities
Some readers note the advice can feel challenging or confrontational to those deeply ingrained in pleasing behaviors
comparable_titles: The Disease to Please by Harriet B. Braiker
When I Say No, I Feel Guilty by Manuel J. Smith
The Assertiveness Workbook by Randy J. Paterson
Set Boundaries, Find Peace by Nedra Glover Tawwab
